#### 2. Demo Management Lacks Organization

 Supademo doesn’t offer structured folders or tagging, making it hard to organize multiple demos.
 Finding, updating, or repurposing older demos can be time-consuming and frustrating.
 As your business scales, managing demos efficiently becomes a challenge.

‍

#### 3. Missing Features That Limit Functionality

 Supademo lacks multi-path demo flows, deep CRM integrations, and advanced analytics dashboards.
 Businesses looking for detailed engagement tracking might find its capabilities too basic.
 If you need more flexibility and data insights, these missing features could be a dealbreaker.

#### 4. Limited Customization for Branding [...] ### Cons of Supademo:

- Limited Customization (for some): While offering many customization options, some users might find limitations in deeply altering UI elements compared to platforms with full HTML/CSS control over every aspect.
- Demo Management: For users creating a very large volume of demos, the organizational features might feel less robust than some enterprise-focused platforms, though team workspaces address some of this.
- Recording Issues/Bugs (occasional): Some users have reported occasional glitches or lags during recording or playback, though this is common feedback for many screen capture tools.

‍

## What Do Users Not Like About Supademo? [...] ### Pros of Supademo

- Ease of Use and Speed: Highly rated for its user-friendly interface and rapid demo creation, often in minutes. It's designed to be intuitive, even for non-technical users.
- AI-Powered Features: Leverages generative AI for synthetic voiceovers in multiple languages, automatic text annotations for hotspots, and instant demo translation (15+ languages).
- Versatile Recording Options: Supports HTML, screenshot, and video-based interactive demos for web applications, desktop applications, and mobile apps (via screenshot uploads).

Title: Navattic vs Supademo: Which Demo Tool Wins? | Naoma
Naoma, the AI sales agent. Naoma is your future sales agent. Navattic vs Supademo in 2026: HTML fidelity vs published pricing, Agent Demos vs the AI Demo Agent, G2 data — an honest read from a competitor. * Navattic and Supademo are both top-rated interactive demo platforms, and the trade between them is clean: Navattic offers deeper HTML capture and a more enterprise-polished motion but renders no prices and bills annually or quarterly only, while Supademo publishes every number from $38 per creator per month, offers monthly billing, and sells entirely self-serve. * Navattic's edge is fidelity and packaging: pixel-true HTML capture on every tier including free, three named Navattic Agents shipped in March 2026, and SOC 2 Type II, ISO 27001, and HIPAA behind a sales-assisted purchase. * Supademo's edge is the buying experience: a free plan, a 14-day trial, checkout without a call, and a credit-metered AI Demo Agent (GA June 2026) you can test against 1,500 free credits. * G2 has them close as of August 2026: Navattic at 4.8 with about 1,057 reviews in the August snapshot, Supademo at 4.7 with 626 — complaints cluster on analytics depth and learning curve for Navattic, missing features and customization limits for Supademo. results.title: Supademo Review 2026: Interactive Tours vs AI Demo Videos | Demosmith Blog
results.content:
Limited customisation and branding on lower tiers. The free plan includes Supademo branding on all demos. Even on Pro, branding options are more limited than what Storylane or Navattic offer. Users who need pixel-perfect brand consistency across demos find this frustrating.
 Screenshot-only capture on Pro. HTML capture requires the Scale plan at $38 per creator per month. Teams that need interactive elements beyond click-through screenshots must pay 40% more per seat. Several reviewers mention upgrading solely for HTML capture and feeling the jump is steep for a single feature. [...] Voiceover limitations. Supademo offers AI-generated voiceover, but users report limited voice options and less natural-sounding output compared to dedicated voiceover tools. For teams that want polished narration on their demos, this is an area where the tool falls short.
 No offline demos or demo centres. You cannot download demos for offline use (trade shows, conferences without reliable Wi-Fi). And Supademo lacks a demo centre feature for organising multiple demos into a branded library that prospects can browse on their own. [...] Missing integrations that enterprise buyers expect. Supademo integrates with HubSpot, Salesforce, and Slack, but lacks connections to Marketo, Segment, and several other marketing automation platforms. Teams running complex lead scoring or multi-touch attribution find themselves exporting data manually.
 No sandbox or demo environment cloning. Unlike Walnut or Reprise, Supademo does not create a live sandbox of your product. You get screenshots or HTML snapshots, not a functioning copy of your application. For enterprise sales teams running personalised demo environments, this is a non-starter.
